summary: M2-S05 (type access) built as one SharingRules container file plus its manifest and two notes. One criteria-based rule, Support_Cases_To_Tier_2: RecordTypeId equals Support, includeRecordsOwnedByAll true, Edit to the Support_Tier_2 public group built in M2-S04. No Sharing.settings file and no OWD written here - the Private sharingModel stays on M1-S01's Case.object-meta.xml (v4 blocker B01). No rule targets the Billing record type or Billing_Team, per assumption A1 and this step's declared manual acceptance test. Four declared outputs written, nothing undeclared, all cited checkers exit 0 on the first pass, check-outputs ok.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 MEDIUM row: the step declares an output whose shape the cited skills document by worked example rather than by element table for the two values that matter most. (1) criteriaItems.value for a RecordTypeId criterion is written as the bare developer name 'Support' on the strength of admin/duplicate-management's worked example, which carries an explicit UNVERIFIED marker saying the guide does not establish whether the field takes a developer name or an 18-character Id. (2) The package.xml type name is the container form (SharingRules:Case), which two library skills document and this step's declared manifest test names, while the step's own primary cited skill recommends the rule-type form (SharingCriteriaRule:Case.Support_Cases_To_Tier_2). Every element NAME and every enum value traces to the Step 3 inventory, every cited checker exited 0 on the first pass, check-outputs is ok, and no Questions-to-Ask row was answered by an undocumented default - so nothing here is a LOW condition.

process_observations.observation: The plan's own v4 blocker B01 was already correct on disk: no settings/Sharing.settings-meta.xml is declared, and the Private OWD this rule is measured against sits on M1-S01's Case.object-meta.xml, which is exactly where the cited skill says sharingModel lives ('Both live on the CustomObject file, not in a separate settings file').

The step's checker test was widened to build scope with a reproduced negative recorded in the plan, so the exit code stands for something: at step scope the checker resolves 0 object OWDs and passes vacuously, at build scope it resolves 1 and would fire HIGH if the grant were not above the default.

Two skills in the library manifest a SharingRules file by its container type with an object member, and one - the skill this step actually cites - says in bold that the container 'is not what you address' and to manifest SharingCriteriaRule with Object.RuleName members; the library therefore documents two incompatible manifest shapes for the same file with no note reconciling them.

Support_Tier_2 carries doesIncludeBosses=true (set in M2-S04 and labelled a skill default there), which the gotchas file says 'applies retroactively to every rule that ever targets it' - so the Edit grant this step writes will silently travel up the role hierarchy the day one is loaded, and no clarification asks whether that is wanted.

The invoking instruction described this step as 'the criteria-based sharing rule(s) that let Billing see Billing cases', while the step's declared manual acceptance test asserts the opposite - that the only rule shares Support cases to Support_Tier_2 and that no rule names the Billing record type or Billing_Team; the plan was followed and Billing's own access is carried by queue ownership from M2-S04, but the two readings should be reconciled before the M2 gate.

The RecordTypeId criterion value format is UNVERIFIED in the library's own words - the guide does not establish whether the field takes a record type developer name or an 18-character Id - and this build has no org to settle it, so the bare developer name 'Support' was written with the marker carried into deploy-order.md decision 3 beside the fix order rather than buried in a well-architected note.
The molecular tests this step declares have not been run by their owner; this agent ran the same checker for its own repair loop only.
